analysis.title: How can I invest in transformational innovation? (UBS House View Briefcase)
key_insights: UBS CIO recommends complementing diversified equity portfolios with targeted exposure to three transformational themes: AI, Power and resources, and Longevity.

AI-related capex is estimated to reach USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027, with agentic AI supporting the next phase. Hyperscalers have raised 2026 capex estimates and project further increases in 2027.

Elevated expectations, post-midterm policy uncertainty, and diverging company outcomes raise the risk of single-stock concentration in AI. UBS favors balanced exposure across the AI value chain: select semiconductors and hardware, megacap tech, and more defensive areas.
AI-linked stocks were volatile last week as investors assessed NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's surprise departure, adding to questions on AI valuations and the outlook for sustained data center investment.

Data center demand is accelerating power and grid investment, with annual sector investment expected to reach USD 3tr by 2030. Opportunities span grid resilience, renewables, nuclear, industrial automation, and critical minerals.
Data centers could account for up to 9% of total US electricity use by 2035, versus around 4% currently, based on Bloomberg New Energy Finance forecasts.
Power and resources risks are US policy shifts, execution risks, and project delays. UBS cites robust investment pipelines and strong order backlogs as support for the longer-term outlook.

UBS is constructive on obesity treatments as greater supply and lower pricing broaden patient access. It forecasts global GLP-1 revenue growth of 12% per year on average through 2030, driven by adoption, benefits beyond weight loss, expanding insurance coverage, and more oral GLP-1s.

Multiple late-stage trial results in cancer, cardio-metabolic conditions, and neurology over the coming months could be catalysts for Longevity. Global longevity market revenue is estimated at USD 8tr annually by 2030, up from USD 5.3tr in 2023.

sector_views.rationale: AI capex is rising to USD 1.4tr in 2027 and AI remains a driver of earnings growth. UBS favors diversified exposure across the value chain given concentration risk.
Data center demand is driving power and grid investment toward USD 3tr annually by 2030, supported by order backlogs.
Obesity drug adoption and late-stage clinical readouts support long-term growth. Global longevity market revenue is estimated at USD 8tr by 2030.

earnings_insights: AI investment remains a driver of earnings growth, per UBS CIO. Investors are increasingly focused on adoption, monetization, US policy, and returns on capital.

trade_ideas.description: Long diversified, targeted exposure to AI, Power and resources, and Longevity as a complement to broader equity portfolios
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural trends should remain a key differentiator for equity market performance over the long run.
trade_ideas.risk: Single-stock concentration, elevated expectations, post-midterm policy uncertainty, execution risks and project delays.

risk_factors: Single-stock concentration in AI given elevated expectations and diverging company outcomes.
Post-midterm US policy uncertainty and shifting US policy.
Questions on AI adoption, monetization, and returns on capital.
Execution risks and project delays in power and grid buildout, with data center buildout adjusting.
Surprise departure of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang adding to AI valuation questions.

geopolitical: Post-midterm US policy uncertainty and shifting US policy are cited as risks for AI and for Power and resources.
